analysis.one_liner: Indian Oil Corporation is India's largest state-run oil company, refining crude oil and marketing petrol, diesel, LPG and other fuels across the country.
analysis.whats_happening: IOC's board meets around October 30, 2026 (about two weeks away) to approve Q2 FY27 results. This follows a Q1 FY27 (April-June 2026) standalone net loss of roughly ₹2,661 crore, a sharp reversal from a ₹6,808 crore profit a year earlier and an ₹11,377 crore profit the previous quarter. Separately, the government made Aadhaar e-KYC mandatory for LPG subsidy from October 1, 2026, with about 3.16 crore consumers still unverified and a Delhi High Court case pending (next hearing November 18, 2026).
analysis.plain_terms: IOC buys crude oil, refines it, and sells fuel - but it doesn't fully control its selling price, especially for cooking gas, where prices are influenced by government policy. That means its profit can swing wildly between quarters depending on crude oil price moves and refining margins, even when nothing about the underlying business has changed. This quarter was a loss; the quarter before was a large profit - that volatility is normal for this industry, not evidence the business is failing. The real question for investors is whether the government compensates IOC when it sells LPG below cost, and the timing of that is uncertain.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026 qtr): standalone net loss of about ₹2,661-2,662 crore versus a ₹6,808 crore profit a year ago and an ₹11,377-15,176 crore profit in the immediately preceding quarter (Q4 FY26, figures vary slightly by source). Sources attribute the loss to inventory devaluation as crude prices moved, compressed marketing margins, and LPG under-recovery, but the exact gross refining margin and crude cost figures circulating for this quarter contradict each other - one figure (crude basket of ~$100/barrel) does not match independently known averages (~$83/barrel) for the period, so treat specific GRM numbers as Not verified - check on Screener or IOC's investor presentation directly. For FY26 as a whole, standalone net profit was ₹36,802 crore versus ₹12,962 crore in FY25 - a large jump that likely reflects favourable crude/inventory swings during the year rather than a structural improvement in the core business, so it shouldn't be read as a clean growth trend.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 28.9% from its February 2026 peak of ₹183.5 to the current ₹130.38, a decline that lines up with the Q1 FY27 loss and a broader correction in oil marketing stocks rather than a one-off shock. Over 1 year the stock is down 10.66%, close to the Nifty's -9.53% and peer BPCL's -8.29% - this looks like a sector-wide move, not IOC-specific weakness. Over longer periods IOC has done well: +67.2% over 3 years and +93.29% over 5 years, both comfortably ahead of the Nifty (+16.83% and +25.27%), though it has lagged BPCL over 3 years (+94.33%). The company's history includes several stock splits (most recently 1.5x in June 2022); these are already reflected in the adjusted price series and are not a source of understated returns, unlike a demerger would be.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of about 5.5x and P/B of about 0.84x, IOC looks statistically cheap, especially against an ROE of 20.5% and ROCE of 18.7%. Why it's cheap: oil marketing companies typically trade at low multiples because earnings are volatile (tied to refining margins and crude cycles), because the government can impose retail price controls on fuels like LPG with little notice, and because refining is a capital-intensive, low structural-growth business. Whether it is genuinely cheap is less clear, because the trailing P/E is built on FY26 profit that was likely flattered by favourable crude/inventory movements - a more 'normalised' earnings base could imply a higher effective multiple.
analysis.growth_read: Reported revenue and profit growth in FY26 is driven mainly by crude price pass-through and refining margin swings rather than higher sales volumes, which is typical for a commodity refiner-marketer. The company's actual expansion push is in petrochemicals - a reported ~₹1 trillion capex plan over five years, including the Paradip PX-PTA complex, plus a recently approved ₹2,449 crore gas pipeline project. Until petrochemical capacity scales up, investors should read IOC's growth as margin/price-cycle-led rather than volume-led, which is less durable.
analysis.health_read: Debt-to-equity has improved to roughly 0.6-0.7x from about 0.93x five years ago, a genuine deleveraging trend, and returns on capital remain healthy (ROE 20.5%, ROCE 18.7%). The bigger concern for IOC is not financial risk from debt but business-model risk: profits depend heavily on crude price swings, refining margins, and government-controlled LPG pricing, which can turn a strong quarter into a loss quarter with little warning. Exact operating cash flow conversion for the recent quarters was not independently verified - check on Screener.
analysis.ownership_read: The promoter is the President of India (Government of India) at 51.50%, unchanged for five straight quarters, and there is no pledging to report, as is standard for a state-owned enterprise. FII holding slipped from 9.84% to 9.08% over the latest quarter while DII holding rose from 9.1% to 9.52%. No well-known individual or marquee investor appears on the shareholding register.
strengths: Dividend yield of 6.33% (TTM dividend ₹8.25) with a consistent PSU dividend track record
ROE of 20.5% and ROCE of 18.7% despite being a capital-intensive refining business
Debt-to-equity improved to roughly 0.6-0.7x from about 0.93x five years ago
Outperformed the Nifty by a wide margin over 3 years (+67.2% vs +16.83%) and 5 years (+93.29% vs +25.27%)
watchpoints: Standalone net loss of about ₹2,661 crore in Q1 FY27, a sharp swing from an ₹11,377 crore profit the prior quarter - earnings are highly volatile quarter to quarter
LPG under-recovery and the new mandatory Aadhaar e-KYC rule from October 2026 affect roughly 3.16 crore consumers, with a Delhi High Court case pending (hearing November 18, 2026)
Exact gross refining margin and crude cost figures for the loss quarter could not be reliably verified - one widely circulated crude-basket figure appears inconsistent with independent data
Stock is down 28.9% from its February 2026 peak, broadly tracking a sector-wide decline in oil marketing stocks rather than a company-specific issue
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 results due around October 30, 2026 - these will show whether the Q1 loss was a one-off inventory/crude-price blip (brokerage ICICI Securities reportedly expects a swing back to roughly ₹7,303 crore profit) or a sign of sustained margin pressure.
analysis.data_notes: P/E, P/B, ROE, ROCE, debt-to-equity and shareholding pattern were cross-checked against Screener.in and Trendlyne-type sources and were broadly consistent. Q1 FY27 figures diverge between standalone and consolidated reporting across sources, and one source's quarterly crude-basket price ($100.74/barrel) contradicts independently known averages (~$83/barrel) for the same period, so the exact gross refining margin and inventory-loss quantum for the quarter are Not verified - check IOC's investor presentation or concall transcript on bseindia.com or iocl.com directly. Operating cash flow conversion was not independently verified.
